name: craft
description: Software craftsmanship discipline skills: grill (the interview primitive — walk a decision tree one question at a time, facts looked up rather than asked, no acting until shared understanding), grill-with-docs (that loop applied to vocabulary, against per-repo CONTEXT.md glossaries), diagnose, prototype, tdd, improve-codebase-architecture, grok (stateful multi-session codebase comprehension with supersession-aware understanding records), zoom-out (adapted in part from mattpocock/skills, MIT), infra-review (architecture/security review of Terraform+Atlantis PRs), quiz-me (opt-in active-recall comprehension check after a code explanation), interrogate-model (holistic representability review of a domain model — the legitimate scenarios and personas it cannot express), design-by-stories (design an artifact's shape — schema, template, data model, config — by modeling its actors and user stories first, then deriving the shape from the stories), and lucid-architecture-diagram (drive AWS cloud architecture diagrams in Lucid, including the two silent-failure modes of its API). derive-conventions (derive a repo's unwritten house style from its own code, adjudicate each inferred rule with the human, and write the approved set to CONVENTIONS.md so the review agents stop re-deriving it). Three read-only post-edit review agents ride along, each deriving the host repository's conventions rather than importing preferences: house-style-reviewer (a diff against the repo's own unlinted conventions, skipping whatever its linters already enforce), comment-reviewer (docstrings against the code they describe, including comments left unchanged while the code beneath them moved), and copy-reviewer (user-facing strings against the voice the product already uses). Composes with spec-flow and ndr plugins.

interface.longDescription: Reusable software craftsmanship workflows for design, diagnosis, testing, review, and comprehension.
